newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy government calls confidence votes on budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy government calls confidence votes on budget.

text.p: The Italian government called three confidence votes in the Senate (upper house) on Friday to sweep aside some 3,000 opposition amendments blocking passage of the 1997 budget.

Civil service minister Franco Bassanini told the assembly that the centre-left government was calling the votes "with regret" after opposition senators refused to withdraw the avalanche of amendments.
The budget bill, designed to slash 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) from next year's deficit, is vital to Italy's hopes of joining Europe's planned single currency.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's cabinet has said the parliamentary timetable for the budget's passage, envisaged in the Senate by December 19, would be impossible if all the amendments had to be voted on.
Bassanini told senators that the government was submitting three so-called umbrella amendments grouping all the articles of the budget bill and was putting them to confidence votes.

The Senate session was suspended after his announcement so parliamentary party leaders could decide when the votes would take place. Prodi has a comfortable majority in the Senate and his expected victory will sweep aside the blocking amendments.
